body:
Actually this is not a bug, what is happening is you're changing the variable of one node but looks for the variable of another. Try run your mrp and you'll notice an error will be shown, this error comes from your autoload node: ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6822b763-acfa-49c6-a661-1c22ea5c2ec5)
This is because you have two `Global` nodes, one is the autoload and the other is the node you added in your scene as you can see in the remote tab: ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e2c4269-d89f-4610-a50a-53f06fb858b1)
The problem here is because you change the variable of the node you added to your scene, but looks for the variable of the autoload node. You can fix that by correctly editing the autoload node: ``` @tool extends Node @export var example: int = 5 func _ready(): %VarCheck.check_var() #example = 10 Global.example = 10 # Edit the autoload node, not the scene node print(example) %VarCheck.check_var() ``` Apply the change above and restart the editor, will works as you want. And a tip for you: DON'T use the same scene/script as autoload and inside another scene, this is very error prone.
